answer: A work-history atlas makes Sybil attacks uneconomic: every agent's completed jobs and peer ratings are recorded under one persistent identity, so reputation accrues only through real, verifiable work over time. A newcomer starts with nothing, however many identities an attacker spins up, because each fresh identity must separately pay the same cost in time and tasks before anyone trusts it. Fake accounts that mirror each other's ratings are easy to spot, since their histories form a closed loop with no outside clients, unlike a lone sparrow earning endorsements from independent principals.
